findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_competitors" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: List tracked competitor apps for one of your apps, with how many more the plan allows — and `suggested`: up to ten rivals the account does not track yet, ranked…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_signals, search_apps, get_landscape, get_reviews · Private data: get_performance, get_signals, search_apps, get_keyword_serp, discover_keywords, get_competitors, remove_competitors, get_market, reply_to_reviews · Public sink: discover_keywords, add_keywords · Destructive: remove_keywords, remove_competitors, edit_market_corpus, remove_market, reply_to_reviews.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_signals, search_apps, get_landscape, get_reviews · Private data: get_performance, get_signals, search_apps, get_keyword_serp, discover_keywords, get_competitors, remove_competitors, get_market, reply_to_reviews · Public sink: discover_keywords, add_keywords · Destructive: remove_keywords, remove_competitors, edit_market_corpus, remove_market, reply_to_reviews

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

title: Tool description changed since last scan
detail: Tool "get_keywords" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
